speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by describing the pain to me—when did it begin, and is it sharp or dull? Also, have you noticed any swelling or redness in the affected wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the radiation of pain to the elbow and your mother's history of rheumatoid arthritis, could you describe whether you experience morning stiffness in your hands or any swelling in other joints besides the right wrist? Also, have you noticed any tingling or numbness in your thumb, index, or middle fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous assessment of gastroenteritis does not align with your wrist pain and maternal history of autoimmune disease; we need to focus on the musculoskeletal symptoms. Did your pain worsen specifically when bending your thumb back toward your palm or when gripping your son, and have you noticed any weakness in your grip strength? REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of right wrist and thumb.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is puzzling that the ultrasound shows normal readings despite your report of pain radiating to the elbow and a history of a fall; could you describe if the pain is worse at night or if you notice any clicking or locking in the thumb joint? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right wrist and thumb. Also, do you have any numbness or tingling in your thumb or index finger? REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray right wrist and thumb.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis (with atypical radiation or possible concurrent cervical radiculopathy). The normal imaging rules out fracture or significant arthritis; the pain with gripping/holding an infant and location in the thumb/wrist strongly suggest tendonitis despite the lack of swelling.
